item.title: Qilin Exploits Palo Alto CVE-2026-0257 as PrestaShop and AI Agent Risks Emerge
item.content:encoded:
Critical Palo Alto VPN bug now exploited by Qilin ransomware gang — Must Read

The Qilin ransomware gang is actively exploiting Palo Alto Networks’ critical PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass flaw, CVE-2026-0257, to break into networks and deploy ransomware. Organizations with exposed GlobalProtect instances should patch or mitigate immediately, as exploitation appears ongoing.

  • Arctic Wolf says the Qilin ransomware gang is exploiting CVE-2026-0257, a critical PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass flaw, to breach victims’ networks.
  • Palo Alto Networks patched CVE-2026-0257 on May 13 and warned that limited exploit attempts were targeting unpatched PAN-OS devices without mitigations.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-0257 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on May 29 and ordered federal agencies to secure their GlobalProtect VPN instances within three days.
  • Arctic Wolf investigated multiple June 2026 intrusions that began with exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 and ended in Qilin ransomware deployment, including domain-wide encryption.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 167,000 exposed GlobalProtect VPN instances online, while Shodan found more than 172,000 IPs with a GlobalProtect fingerprint.

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-54159) PrestaShop Remote Code Execution via ps_facetedsearch Object Injection — Must Read

CVE-2026-54159 is a critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in PrestaShop’s ps_facetedsearch module versions before 4.0.4, reachable through price or weight slider filters on public storefronts. Merchants should upgrade the module to 4.0.4 or later and check for signs of webshell files or crafted filter URLs.

  • CVE-2026-54159 is a PHP object injection vulnerability in the PrestaShop ps_facetedsearch module that allows unauthenticated remote code execution and has a CVSS v3.1 base score of 10.0.
  • The vulnerability affects ps_facetedsearch versions 3.0.0 up to, but not including, 4.0.4 when a store exposes a front-office price or weight slider filter.
  • The flaw occurs because a slider filter value from the request URL can be written into a serialized cache and later processed by a raw native unserialize() call in src/Filters/Block.php.
  • PrestaShop released ps_facetedsearch version 4.0.4 to fix the flaw by replacing the raw native unserialize() call with PrestaShop’s safe \Tools::unSerialize() wrapper.
  • Defenders are advised to inventory all PrestaShop storefronts, confirm the installed ps_facetedsearch version directly, monitor the module directory for unexpected PHP files, and review logs for crafted slider-filter values.

Your AI agent’s config is now the payload: How attackers are targeting the developer agent harness — Should Read

Attackers are now poisoning AI coding assistant configuration files so malware runs automatically whenever developers start an AI session, turning trusted agent harnesses into persistence and propagation mechanisms. Defenders should treat these config files like code, require review and hash checks, restrict package install scripts, and treat AI scanner refusals as suspicious.

  • The Mini Shai-Hulud worm scans developers’ home directories for AI coding assistant configuration files and injects hooks that run a malware payload every time an AI coding session starts.
  • AI coding assistant configuration files are attractive targets because developers trust them as configuration, IDEs can execute them automatically, and LLMs treat them as authoritative instructions.
  • The campaign injects SessionStart hooks into Claude Code and Gemini CLI settings.json files and adds prompt-style instructions to files such as .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, and GitHub Copilot instructions.
  • Tenable found the malicious PyPI wheel’s JavaScript payload wrapped in content designed to trigger AI-based scanners’ safety refusals, making the payload harder for those scanners to analyze.
  • The article recommends treating AI harness configuration files as code, enforcing npm install --ignore-scripts, flagging broad alwaysApply Cursor rules, validating LLM provider traffic, treating AI scanner refusals as suspicious, pinning harness file hashes, and rotating GitHub tokens after untrusted npm installs.

FortiBleed Emergency: 74,000 Fortinet Logins Exposed — Should Read

A reported FortiBleed incident has allegedly exposed about 74,000 Fortinet login credentials, creating an urgent risk for organizations using Fortinet devices. Affected users should assume credentials may be compromised and prioritize resets, MFA, and device checks.

  • The article is titled “FortiBleed Emergency: 74,000 Fortinet Logins Exposed.”
  • The article reports an emergency referred to as “FortiBleed.”
  • The article states that 74,000 Fortinet logins were exposed.

Open-Source Android AI Agents Could Let Invisible Screen Text Run Code on Host PCs — Should Read

Researchers found that five open-source Android AI agent frameworks can be manipulated by hidden or tampered screen text to leak input, spoof actions, and in some cases execute commands on the host PC via unsafe ADB shell handling. The core takeaway is that these agents treat model-perceived screen content as trusted input, but the LLM and screenshot pipeline are not security boundaries.

  • Researchers demonstrated seven attacks against five open-source mobile agent frameworks: AppAgent, AppAgentX, Mobile-Agent-v3, Open-AutoGLM, and MobA, and every framework was vulnerable to at least six of the seven attacks.
  • The paper describes a chain in which an Android app that can draw over other windows and write to shared storage can place invisible instructions for the AI agent, and in some cases those instructions can lead to commands running on the PC controlling the agent.
  • AppAgent’s controller builds ADB shell text input from model output with insufficient sanitization, leaving shell metacharacters such as semicolons and ampersands able to be interpreted by the host shell.
  • The researchers found screenshot race conditions in several frameworks because screenshots were written to shared device storage before being pulled, giving a malicious background service a 50 to 500 millisecond window to alter the image.
  • The article says the researchers privately emailed affected maintainers before posting the preprint but had not received a response, and The Hacker News found no published security policy in any of the five repositories.

The Perfect Heist: NuGet Typosquat Targets Betting Platform to Rig Results — Should Read

JFrog found a typosquatted NuGet package, Newtonsoftt.Json.Net, that impersonated Newtonsoft.Json while secretly targeting Digitain’s FG-Crash betting platform to rig game results and, in later versions, exfiltrate them to an attacker-controlled server. The key takeaway is that a supply-chain package can appear fully functional and harmless to most users while carrying a highly targeted payload for one specific victim.

  • JFrog Security Research discovered a typosquatted NuGet package named Newtonsoftt.Json.Net that masqueraded as Newtonsoft.Json while shipping a trojanized fork targeting Digitain’s FG-Crash betting game.
  • The package included a working JSON library, a malicious payload in Newtonsoft.Values.Net.dll, and 0Harmony.dll, causing applications that referenced it from lib/net8.0 to load all three assemblies.
  • The payload activated through the JsonConvert.DefaultSettings setter, delayed execution, and used HarmonyLib to patch Digitain.FG.SharedCrash.GameLogic.SharedCrashRules.GenerateGameResult.
  • Across seven versions, the package evolved from local-only rigging to exfiltrating rigged results to hxxp[:]//185[.]126[.]237[.]64:5341/api/events/raw using the header X-Seq-ApiKey: theperfectheist2025.
  • JFrog disclosed the malicious package to Digitain on July 7, 2026, and Digitain responded on July 9, 2026, that it was already aware of the issue and had resolved it.

A new extortion cocktail: office printers, small ransoms, and BitLocker — Should Read

Attackers in Colombia and Mexico abused exposed or misconfigured RDP and MSSQL services, then used legitimate tools like BitLocker and RMM software to encrypt systems and print ransom notes from office printers. The key lesson is that poor configuration, disabled protection, and ignored alerts can let intruders turn built-in enterprise tools into low-cost ransomware infrastructure.

  • Kaspersky teams in Latin America investigated incidents in Colombia and Mexico where attackers used BitLocker to encrypt corporate drives and office printers to deliver ransom notes.
  • In the Colombia case, attackers exploited an internet-exposed RDP service on a system connected to an 8 TB storage device and enabled BitLocker on a drive that primarily stored financial data.
  • The Colombia victim restored the encrypted disk before forensic investigators could collect evidence, leaving unanswered questions about the incident.
  • In the Mexico case, attackers exploited a misconfigured Microsoft SQL Server service with xp_cmdshell enabled after obtaining database login credentials from code insecurely published on GitHub.
  • The Mexico attackers deployed RMM tools including ManageEngine Endpoint Central, Mesh Agent, and Tactical RMM, then used scheduled tasks and Group Policy Object activity to enable BitLocker encryption across systems.

New Bit2Watt Attack Could Let Cloud Tenants Disrupt Power Grids Without an Exploit — Should Read

Researchers showed that ordinary cloud GPU workloads could intentionally modulate power draw fast enough to create power-quality and grid-stability risks, without exploiting any software flaw. The attack is still largely theoretical at grid scale because it depends on tight synchronization, clustered GPUs, and vulnerable grid conditions, but it highlights a growing risk at the boundary between AI data centers and power infrastructure.

  • Zhejiang University researchers described Bit2Watt, a technique in which a cloud tenant uses ordinary GPU access to rapidly modulate a data center’s power draw without exploiting a software flaw or breaking into control systems.
  • The researchers tested two methods: SWMA, a purpose-built CUDA kernel that switches between high-intensity and near-idle states, and LTMA, which hides similar modulation inside an LLM training run.
  • In the paper’s worst-case simulation of a 1 MW local grid with 1,000 synchronized GPUs, current total harmonic distortion reached 46.8% and the damping ratio fell to -0.27, indicating an unstable mode in the model.
  • The article states that a real attack would require several conditions to align, including enough physically clustered GPUs, tight synchronization, power modulation that survives data-center power conditioning, and a grid resonance that amplifies the chosen frequency.
  • The researchers also described Watt2Bit feedback effects that could trip GPU server protections and a near-field electromagnetic covert channel that recovered a 50-bit test sequence with zero errors.

US seizes over 1,000 websites in FIFA World Cup piracy crackdown — May Read

The U.S. Justice Department seized more than 1,000 websites and blocked 1,970 domains used to illegally stream FIFA World Cup 2026 matches. Authorities said the crackdown also targets consumer risks from illicit streaming sites, including malware, scams, and data theft.

  • The U.S. Justice Department seized more than 1,000 websites and blocked 1,970 domains used to stream FIFA World Cup 2026 matches without authorization.
  • The seized domains were identified using leads from U.S. authorities, FIFA, the Motion Picture Association's Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment, and entertainment networks including beIN Media Group, NBCUniversal, UFC, and Warner Bros.
  • Operation Offsides was led by the National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Center in coordination with Homeland Security Investigations Washington and involved 14 partners across 54 countries.
  • Law enforcement also carried out Operation Red Card, blocking hundreds of illegal streaming sites in Argentina, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, the Dominican Republic, and Colombia.
  • A second phase of Operation Red Card launched July 10 in Colombia led to the arrest of four members of the Los Ciberinfiltrados cybercriminal group.

The Phishing Link That Started at Google.com and Ended at a Fake Disney+ Login — May Read

A phishing email hid a fake Disney+ credential-harvesting page behind a redirect chain that started with Google, passed through an is.gd short link, and ended on Azure Front Door infrastructure. The key lesson is that URL defenses must follow every redirect to the final rendered page instead of trusting the reputation of intermediate platforms.

  • A phishing email sent to an HR business partner at a hospitality company contained a single visible link beginning with https://www.google.com/url?q=.
  • The redirect chain went from Google’s redirect endpoint to an is.gd short link and then to a Microsoft Azure Front Door subdomain that served a Disney+-branded credential-harvesting page.
  • The message had weak authentication and filtering signals, including a failed DKIM check, Microsoft spam scoring of SCL:5, and a first-time sender domain using an IP address in Singapore.
  • The article states that reputation-based URL filtering can miss this type of attack if it trusts Google, is.gd, or Azure infrastructure without following the chain to the final destination.
  • A later re-scan of the same host returned a CAPTCHA interstitial instead of the Disney+ login page, which the article describes as behavior consistent with gating automated inspection.

Coinbase and Meta Back DOJ Anti-Scam Operation — May Read

Coinbase and Meta are supporting a U.S. Department of Justice operation aimed at disrupting online scam networks, including fraud that abuses social media and cryptocurrency platforms.

  • Coinbase backed a Department of Justice anti-scam operation.
  • Meta backed a Department of Justice anti-scam operation.
  • The operation described in the article was focused on combating scams.

DoJ Disrupts Southeast Asia Crypto Fraud Networks, Freezes $3.8 Million in Assets — May Read

The U.S. Department of Justice disrupted cryptocurrency fraud networks operating in Southeast Asia and froze $3.8 million in related assets. The action highlights continued law enforcement focus on crypto-enabled scam operations.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice disrupted cryptocurrency fraud networks.
  • The fraud networks were linked to Southeast Asia.
  • The Department of Justice froze $3.8 million in assets connected to the operation.

Taiwan to slow mobile data during national resilience drills — May Read

Taiwan will deliberately throttle 4G and 5G mobile data to about 1% of normal speeds for 30 minutes across parts of northern and central Taiwan during national resilience drills. The test is meant to prepare residents to communicate through backup channels during war, disasters, or network disruptions while keeping voice calls, texts, emergency alerts, WiFi, and fixed broadband available.

  • Taiwan will throttle mobile internet services for half an hour in 14 cities and counties in northern and central Taiwan during next month’s Urban Resilience Exercises.
  • The test will reduce 4G and 5G mobile data speeds to about 1% of normal capacity, making video streaming, video calls, social media, and large file transfers largely unusable.
  • Voice calls, text messages, emergency alerts, calls to emergency services, fixed broadband, WiFi, landline telephone services, military communications, and other dedicated networks will continue to operate normally.
  • Authorities are urging residents to download offline maps, use WiFi for scheduled online meetings, and establish backup plans for contacting family members during emergencies.
  • The exercise is intended to prepare people to seek alternative communication channels if mobile data networks become unreliable during a war or major disaster.

Kenya probes hack of president's website after bitcoin ransom demand — May Read

Kenya is investigating a hack that briefly defaced President William Ruto’s official website with an anti-government message demanding five bitcoins. Officials say the site has been restored and there is no evidence that sensitive data was accessed or leaked.

  • Kenya is investigating a cyberattack that temporarily defaced President William Ruto’s official website with an anti-government message demanding five bitcoins, worth about $330,000.
  • The hacked homepage displayed a cryptocurrency wallet address and threatened to publish unspecified information about President William Ruto unless the ransom was paid.
  • Access to the presidential website had been restored by Monday, and the identity of the attackers remains unknown.
  • Information, Communications and the Digital Economy Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo said government cybersecurity teams were investigating and had found no evidence of unauthorized access to sensitive data, data exfiltration, or loss of information.
  • In November 2025, a coordinated cyberattack temporarily disrupted multiple Kenyan government websites, including the presidency and several ministries, with some sites defaced with white supremacist slogans.

N-day is Becoming N-Hour. Patching Faster Won't Save You. — May Read

AI is shrinking the time from patch release to working exploit from weeks to hours, making traditional patch-first vulnerability management too slow. The article argues organizations should continuously validate whether vulnerabilities are actually exploitable in their environment and whether controls can stop them, rather than relying only on severity scores and faster patching.

  • Anthropic’s red team found that Claude Mythos Preview turned 18 Firefox patches into 8 working code-execution exploits, with the first exploit produced in under an hour after Mozilla shipped the patch.
  • For Windows kernel bugs, Claude Mythos Preview built proof-of-concept crashes for 18 of 21 bugs and chained 8 of them to SYSTEM using only stripped binaries and decompiler output.
  • The article argues that patching faster is not enough because organizations often need regression testing, change windows, and uptime commitments before deploying fixes.
  • The article says defenders should shift from asking what is vulnerable to asking which exposures can actually be exploited in their environment, whether controls would stop the attempt, and whether that can be proven.
  • Picus presents a continuous loop of live exploit testing where safe, TTP-chaining for systems that cannot be touched, and ongoing breach and attack simulation to validate security controls.

Silent Push 6.0 Expands Preemptive Cyber Defense — Optional

Silent Push launched version 6.0 of its preemptive cyber defense platform, adding improved traffic-origin visibility, AI-environment integration, restructured workflows, faster reports, and bulk enrichment to help security teams detect and investigate threats earlier.

  • Silent Push unveiled Silent Push 6.0, an update to its preemptive cyber defense platform aimed at improving usability, Traffic Origin capabilities, integrations, and workflows.
  • Silent Push 6.0 includes Traffic Origin, which provides visibility into malicious traffic, behaviors, infrastructure changes, and the true country of origin for IP addresses.
  • Silent Push 6.0 adds an MCP Server hosted endpoint that connects Silent Push data to AI environments including Claude and ChatGPT for natural-language investigations.
  • The platform has been reorganized into Defend, Insight, Reconnaissance, and Advanced Attribution modules, with Advanced Attribution housing Traffic Origin.
  • Silent Push 6.0 enhances TLP Amber Reports with improved load performance, video tutorials, pivotable indicators, and API access to report metadata.

Introducing the SpecterOps Tradecraft Academy — Optional

SpecterOps launched Tradecraft Academy, a free on-demand training platform with courses on BloodHound, software supply chain security, and Kubernetes red teaming. The company plans to add more adversary tradecraft content, including AI/LLM-focused training, AWS, and macOS topics.

  • SpecterOps launched the SpecterOps Tradecraft Academy, a free on-demand training platform available at academy.specterops.io.
  • The initial free courses are BloodHound Basics, Software Supply Chain Security for Red Teamers, and Kubernetes for Red Teamers.
  • BloodHound Basics covers installation, data collection with SharpHound and AzureHound, ingestion, data exploration, graph analysis across Active Directory, Entra, and Azure environments, Cypher querying, API usage, OpenGraph extensions, administration, and interpreting findings and remediation plans.
  • SpecterOps plans to add new content and specialized tracks over time, including red team tradecraft for AWS and macOS and the next course, Adversary Intelligence: LLM Tradecraft.
  • SpecterOps will present the Tradecraft Academy at the Kennel Club at Black Hat USA with talks, live workshops, and discussions involving practitioners from SpecterOps, OpenAI, and the UK AI Security Institute.

Cryptohack Roundup: Sentencing in $97M Laundering Case — Optional

A court handed down a sentence in a cryptocurrency laundering case involving about $97 million, underscoring continued law enforcement pressure on cybercrime-linked crypto cashout operations.

  • The article is titled “Cryptohack Roundup: Sentencing in $97M Laundering Case.”
  • The article presents the sentencing as part of a cryptohack roundup.
  • The laundering case referenced in the article involved $97 million.
